audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Judges / Shoftim remaining-nations test list and first deliverer narratives, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for remaining nations, intermarriage/cultic assimilation, Othniel, Cushan-rishathaim, Ehud's left-handed assassination of Eglon, escape and Moab defeat, and Shamgar's oxgoad notice.

verses.restored: These are nations YHWH left to test Israel by them, all who had not known all wars of Canaan,

familiar.text: Now these are the nations which the LORD left, to prove Israel by them, even as many of Israel as had not known all the wars of Canaan;

modern.text: These are the nations that the LORD left to test all the Israelites who had not known any of the wars in Canaan,

original.text: וְאֵ֤לֶּה הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִנִּ֣יחַ יְהוָ֔ה לְנַסּ֥וֹת בָּ֖ם אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֵ֚ת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא יָדְע֔וּ אֵ֖ת כָּל מִלְחֲמ֥וֹת כְּנָֽעַן

verses.restored: only so generations of children of Israel would know, to teach them war—only those who had not formerly known them:

familiar.text: Only that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them war, at the least such as before knew nothing thereof;

modern.text: if only to teach warfare to the subsequent generations of Israel, especially to those who had not known it formerly:

original.text: רַ֗ק לְמַ֨עַן֙ דַּ֚עַת דֹּר֣וֹת בְּנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְלַמְּדָ֖ם מִלְחָמָ֑ה רַ֥ק אֲשֶׁר לְפָנִ֖ים לֹ֥א יְדָעֽוּם

verses.restored: five rulers of Philistines, all Canaanites, Sidonians, and Hivites dwelling at Mount Lebanon from Mount Baal-hermon as far as Lebo-hamath.

familiar.text: Namely, five lords of the Philistines, and all the Canaanites, and the Sidonians, and the Hivites that dwelt in mount Lebanon, from mount Baalhermon unto the entering in of Hamath.

modern.text: the five rulers of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who lived in the mountains of Lebanon from Mount Baal-hermon to Lebo-hamath.

original.text: חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וְכָל הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ וְהַצִּ֣ידֹנִ֔י וְהַ֣חִוִּ֔י יֹשֵׁ֖ב הַ֣ר הַלְּבָנ֑וֹן מֵהַר֙ בַּ֣עַל חֶרְמ֔וֹן עַ֖ד לְב֥וֹא חֲמָֽת

verses.restored: They were for testing Israel by them, to know whether they would listen to commands of YHWH that he commanded their fathers by hand of Moses.

familiar.text: And they were to prove Israel by them, to know whether they would hearken unto the commandments of the LORD, which he commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.

modern.text: These nations were left to test the Israelites, to find out whether they would keep the commandments of the LORD, which He had given their fathers through Moses.

original.text: וַֽיִּהְי֕וּ לְנַסּ֥וֹת בָּ֖ם אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לָדַ֗עַת הֲיִשְׁמְעוּ֙ אֶת מִצְוֺ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֥ה אֶת אֲבוֹתָ֖ם בְּיַד מֹשֶֽׁה

verses.restored: Children of Israel dwelt in midst of Canaanite, Hittite, Amorite, Perizzite, Hivite, and Jebusite.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel dwelt among the Canaanites, Hittites, and Amorites, and Perizzites, and Hivites, and Jebusites:

modern.text: Thus the Israelites continued to live among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.

original.text: וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יָשְׁב֖וּ בְּקֶ֣רֶב הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֑י הַחִתִּ֤י וְהָֽאֱמֹרִי֙ וְהַפְּרִזִּ֔י וְהַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִֽי

verses.restored: They took their daughters for themselves as wives, and their own daughters they gave to their sons, and they served their gods.

familiar.text: And they took their daughters to be their wives, and gave their daughters to their sons, and served their gods.

modern.text: And they took the daughters of these people in marriage, gave their own daughters to their sons, and served their gods. Othniel

original.text: וַיִּקְח֨וּ אֶת בְּנוֹתֵיהֶ֤ם לָהֶם֙ לְנָשִׁ֔ים וְאֶת בְּנוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם נָתְנ֣וּ לִבְנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיַּעַבְד֖וּ אֶת אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: Children of Israel did evil in eyes of YHWH; they forgot YHWH their Divine and served the Baals and Asherahs.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the LORD, and forgat the LORD their God, and served Baalim and the groves.

modern.text: So the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD; they forgot the LORD their God and served the Baals and the Asherahs.

original.text: וַיַּעֲשׂ֨וּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל אֶת הָרַע֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַֽיִּשְׁכְּח֖וּ אֶת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֑ם וַיַּעַבְד֥וּ אֶת הַבְּעָלִ֖ים וְאֶת הָאֲשֵׁרֽוֹת

verses.restored: Anger of YHWH burned against Israel, and he sold them into hand of Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram-naharaim; children of Israel served Cushan-rishathaim eight years.

familiar.text: Therefore the anger of the LORD was hot against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Chushanrishathaim king of Mesopotamia: and the children of Israel served Chushanrishathaim eight years.

modern.text: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram-naharaim, and the Israelites served him eight years.

original.text: וַיִּֽחַר אַ֤ף יְהוָה֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַֽיִּמְכְּרֵ֗ם בְּיַד֙ כּוּשַׁ֣ן רִשְׁעָתַ֔יִם מֶ֖לֶךְ אֲרַ֣ם נַהֲרָ֑יִם וַיַּעַבְד֧וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶת כּוּשַׁ֥ן רִשְׁעָתַ֖יִם שְׁמֹנֶ֥ה שָׁנִֽים

verses.restored: Children of Israel cried out to YHWH, and YHWH raised a savior/deliverer for children of Israel, and he saved them: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother.

familiar.text: And when the children of Israel cried unto the LORD, the LORD raised up a deliverer to the children of Israel, who delivered them, even Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother.

modern.text: But when the Israelites cried out to the LORD, He raised up Othniel son of Caleb’s younger brother Kenaz as a deliverer to save them.

original.text: וַיִּזְעֲק֤וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל יְהוָ֔ה וַיָּ֨קֶם יְהוָ֥ה מוֹשִׁ֛יעַ לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וַיּֽוֹשִׁיעֵ֑ם אֵ֚ת עָתְנִיאֵ֣ל בֶּן קְנַ֔ז אֲחִ֥י כָלֵ֖ב הַקָּטֹ֥ן מִמֶּֽנּוּ

verses.restored: Spirit of YHWH was upon him, and he judged Israel. He went out to war, and YHWH gave Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram into his hand; his hand prevailed over Cushan-rishathaim.

familiar.text: And the Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel, and went out to war: and the LORD delivered Chushanrishathaim king of Mesopotamia into his hand; and his hand prevailed against Chushanrishathaim.

modern.text: The Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he became Israel’s judge and went out to war. And the LORD delivered Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram into the hand of Othniel, who prevailed against him.

original.text: וַתְּהִ֨י עָלָ֥יו רֽוּחַ יְהוָה֮ וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֣ט אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיֵּצֵא֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וַיִּתֵּ֤ן יְהוָה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ אֶת כּוּשַׁ֥ן רִשְׁעָתַ֖יִם מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֑ם וַתָּ֣עָז יָד֔וֹ עַ֖ל כּוּשַׁ֥ן רִשְׁעָתָֽיִם

verses.restored: Land was quiet forty years. Then Othniel son of Kenaz died.

familiar.text: And the land had rest forty years. And Othniel the son of Kenaz died.

modern.text: So the land had rest for forty years, until Othniel son of Kenaz died. Ehud

original.text: וַתִּשְׁקֹ֥ט הָאָ֖רֶץ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיָּ֖מָת עָתְנִיאֵ֥ל בֶּן קְנַֽז

verses.restored: Children of Israel again did evil in eyes of YHWH, and YHWH strengthened Eglon king of Moab against Israel because they did evil in eyes of YHWH.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the LORD: and the LORD strengthened Eglon the king of Moab against Israel, because they had done evil in the sight of the LORD.

modern.text: Once again the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD. So He gave Eglon king of Moab power over Israel, because they had done evil in the sight of the LORD.

original.text: וַיֹּסִ֨פוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיְחַזֵּ֨ק יְהוָ֜ה אֶת עֶגְל֤וֹן מֶֽלֶךְ מוֹאָב֙ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַ֛ל כִּֽי עָשׂ֥וּ אֶת הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: He gathered to himself sons of Ammon and Amalek; he went and struck Israel, and they possessed city of palms.

familiar.text: And he gathered unto him the children of Ammon and Amalek, and went and smote Israel, and possessed the city of palm trees.

modern.text: After enlisting the Ammonites and Amalekites to join forces with him, Eglon attacked and defeated Israel, taking possession of the City of Palms.

original.text: וַיֶּאֱסֹ֣ף אֵלָ֔יו אֶת בְּנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹן וַעֲמָלֵ֑ק וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּֽירְשׁ֖וּ אֶת עִ֥יר הַתְּמָרִֽים

verses.restored: Children of Israel served Eglon king of Moab eighteen years.

familiar.text: So the children of Israel served Eglon the king of Moab eighteen years.

modern.text: The Israelites served Eglon king of Moab eighteen years.

original.text: וַיַּעַבְד֤וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת עֶגְל֣וֹן מֶֽלֶךְ מוֹאָ֔ב שְׁמוֹנֶ֥ה עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָֽה

verses.restored: Children of Israel cried out to YHWH, and YHWH raised for them a savior/deliverer: Ehud son of Gera, Benjamite, a man bound/restricted in his right hand. Children of Israel sent tribute by his hand to Eglon king of Moab.

familiar.text: But when the children of Israel cried unto the LORD, the LORD raised them up a deliverer, Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite, a man lefthanded: and by him the children of Israel sent a present unto Eglon the king of Moab.

modern.text: And again they cried out to the LORD, and He raised up Ehud son of Gera, a left-handed Benjamite, as their deliverer. So they sent him with tribute to Eglon king of Moab.

original.text: וַיִּזְעֲק֣וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ אֶל יְהוָה֒ וַיָּקֶם֩ יְהוָ֨ה לָהֶ֜ם מוֹשִׁ֗יעַ אֶת אֵה֤וּד בֶּן גֵּרָא֙ בֶּן הַיְמִינִ֔י אִ֥ישׁ אִטֵּ֖ר יַד יְמִינ֑וֹ וַיִּשְׁלְח֨וּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל בְּיָדוֹ֙ מִנְחָ֔ה לְעֶגְל֖וֹן מֶ֥לֶךְ מוֹאָֽב

verses.restored: Ehud made for himself a sword with two edges, a cubit its length, and he strapped it under his garment on his right thigh.

familiar.text: But Ehud made him a dagger which had two edges, of a cubit length; and he did gird it under his raiment upon his right thigh.

modern.text: Now Ehud had made for himself a double-edged sword a cubit long. He strapped it to his right thigh under his cloak

original.text: וַיַּעַשׂ֩ ל֨וֹ אֵה֜וּד חֶ֗רֶב וְלָ֛הּ שְׁנֵ֥י פֵי֖וֹת גֹּ֣מֶד אָרְכָּ֑הּ וַיַּחְגֹּ֤ר אוֹתָהּ֙ מִתַּ֣חַת לְמַדָּ֔יו עַ֖ל יֶ֥רֶךְ יְמִינֽוֹ

verses.restored: He presented tribute to Eglon king of Moab; Eglon was a very fat man.

familiar.text: And he brought the present unto Eglon king of Moab: and Eglon was a very fat man.

modern.text: and brought the tribute to Eglon king of Moab, who was an obese man.

original.text: וַיַּקְרֵב֙ אֶת הַמִּנְחָ֔ה לְעֶגְל֖וֹן מֶ֣לֶךְ מוֹאָ֑ב וְעֶגְל֕וֹן אִ֥ישׁ בָּרִ֖יא מְאֹֽד

verses.restored: It was, when he finished presenting tribute, that he sent away people carrying tribute.

familiar.text: And when he had made an end to offer the present, he sent away the people that bare the present.

modern.text: After Ehud had finished presenting the tribute, he ushered out those who had carried it.

original.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר כִּלָּ֔ה לְהַקְרִ֖יב אֶת הַמִּנְחָ֑ה וַיְשַׁלַּח֙ אֶת הָעָ֔ם נֹשְׂאֵ֖י הַמִּנְחָֽה

verses.restored: But he himself turned back from carved stones/idols near Gilgal and said, A secret word I have for you, O king. He said, Silence. All those standing by him went out from him.

familiar.text: But he himself turned again from the quarries that were by Gilgal, and said, I have a secret errand unto thee, O king: who said, Keep silence. And all that stood by him went out from him.

modern.text: But upon reaching the idols near Gilgal, he himself turned back and said, “I have a secret message for you, O king.” “Silence,” said the king, and all his attendants left him.

original.text: וְה֣וּא שָׁ֗ב מִן הַפְּסִילִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶת הַגִּלְגָּ֔ל וַיֹּ֕אמֶר דְּבַר סֵ֥תֶר לִ֛י אֵלֶ֖יךָ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הָ֔ס וַיֵּֽצְאוּ֙ מֵֽעָלָ֔יו כָּל הָעֹמְדִ֖ים עָלָֽיו

verses.restored: Ehud came to him while he was sitting alone in cool upper chamber. Ehud said, A word of Divine I have for you. He rose from his seat.

familiar.text: And Ehud came unto him; and he was sitting in a summer parlour, which he had for himself alone. And Ehud said, I have a message from God unto thee. And he arose out of his seat.

modern.text: Then Ehud approached him while he was sitting alone in the coolness of his upper room. “I have a word from God for you,” Ehud said, and the king rose from his seat.

original.text: וְאֵה֣וּד בָּ֣א אֵלָ֗יו וְהֽוּא יֹ֠שֵׁב בַּעֲלִיַּ֨ת הַמְּקֵרָ֤ה אֲשֶׁר לוֹ֙ לְבַדּ֔וֹ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵה֔וּד דְּבַר אֱלֹהִ֥ים לִ֖י אֵלֶ֑יךָ וַיָּ֖קָם מֵעַ֥ל הַכִּסֵּֽא

verses.restored: Ehud stretched out his left hand, took sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into his belly.

familiar.text: And Ehud put forth his left hand, and took the dagger from his right thigh, and thrust it into his belly:

modern.text: And Ehud reached with his left hand, pulled the sword from his right thigh, and plunged it into Eglon’s belly.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח אֵהוּד֙ אֶת יַ֣ד שְׂמֹאל֔וֹ וַיִּקַּח֙ אֶת הַחֶ֔רֶב מֵעַ֖ל יֶ֣רֶךְ יְמִינ֑וֹ וַיִּתְקָעֶ֖הָ בְּבִטְנֽוֹ

verses.restored: Even handle went in after blade, and fat closed over blade, for he did not draw sword from his belly; and refuse came out.

familiar.text: And the haft also went in after the blade; and the fat closed upon the blade, so that he could not draw the dagger out of his belly; and the dirt came out.

modern.text: Even the handle sank in after the blade, and Eglon’s fat closed in over it, so that Ehud did not withdraw the sword from his belly. And Eglon’s bowels emptied.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א גַֽם הַנִּצָּ֜ב אַחַ֣ר הַלַּ֗הַב וַיִּסְגֹּ֤ר הַחֵ֨לֶב֙ בְּעַ֣ד הַלַּ֔הַב כִּ֣י לֹ֥א שָׁלַ֛ף הַחֶ֖רֶב מִבִּטְנ֑וֹ וַיֵּצֵ֖א הַֽפַּרְשְׁדֹֽנָה

verses.restored: Ehud went out by porch, shut doors of upper chamber behind him, and locked them.

familiar.text: Then Ehud went forth through the porch, and shut the doors of the parlour upon him, and locked them.

modern.text: Then Ehud went out through the porch, closing and locking the doors of the upper room behind him.

original.text: וַיֵּצֵ֥א אֵה֖וּד הַֽמִּסְדְּר֑וֹנָה וַיִּסְגֹּ֞ר דַּלְת֧וֹת הָעַלִיָּ֛ה בַּעֲד֖וֹ וְנָעָֽל

verses.restored: He went out, and servants came; they saw, and look, doors of upper chamber were locked. They said, Surely he is covering his feet in cool room.

familiar.text: When he was gone out, his servants came; and when they saw that, behold, the doors of the parlour were locked, they said, Surely he covereth his feet in his summer chamber.

modern.text: After Ehud was gone, Eglon’s servants came in and found the doors of the upper room locked. “He must be relieving himself in the cool room,” they said.

original.text: וְה֤וּא יָצָא֙ וַעֲבָדָ֣יו בָּ֔אוּ וַיִּרְא֕וּ וְהִנֵּ֛ה דַּלְת֥וֹת הָעֲלִיָּ֖ה נְעֻל֑וֹת וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אַ֣ךְ מֵסִ֥יךְ ה֛וּא אֶת רַגְלָ֖יו בַּחֲדַ֥ר הַמְּקֵרָֽה

verses.restored: They waited until ashamed, and look, he was not opening doors of upper chamber. They took key and opened, and look, their lord had fallen to ground, dead.

familiar.text: And they tarried till they were ashamed: and, behold, he opened not the doors of the parlour; therefore they took a key, and opened them: and, behold, their lord was fallen down dead on the earth.

modern.text: So they waited until they became worried and saw that he had still not opened the doors of the upper room. Then they took the key and opened the doors—and there was their lord lying dead on the floor.

original.text: וַיָּחִ֣ילוּ עַד בּ֔וֹשׁ וְהְנֵּ֛ה אֵינֶ֥נּוּ פֹתֵ֖חַ דַּלְת֣וֹת הָֽעֲלִיָּ֑ה וַיִּקְח֤וּ אֶת הַמַּפְתֵּ֨חַ֙ וַיִּפְתָּ֔חוּ וְהִנֵּה֙ אֲדֹ֣נֵיהֶ֔ם נֹפֵ֥ל אַ֖רְצָה מֵֽת

verses.restored: Ehud escaped while they delayed; he passed carved stones/idols and escaped to Seirah.

familiar.text: And Ehud escaped while they tarried, and passed beyond the quarries, and escaped unto Seirath.

modern.text: Ehud, however, had escaped while the servants waited. He passed by the idols and escaped to Seirah.

verses.restored: It was, when he came, that he blew shofar in hill country of Ephraim, and children of Israel went down with him from hill country, and he before them.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when he was come, that he blew a trumpet in the mountain of Ephraim, and the children of Israel went down with him from the mount, and he before them.

modern.text: On arriving in Seirah, he blew the ram’s horn throughout the hill country of Ephraim. The Israelites came down with him from the hills, and he became their leader.

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י בְּבוֹא֔וֹ וַיִּתְקַ֥ע בַּשּׁוֹפָ֖ר בְּהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַיֵּרְד֨וּ עִמּ֧וֹ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מִן הָהָ֖ר וְה֥וּא לִפְנֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: He said to them, Pursue after me, for YHWH has given your enemies, Moab, into your hand. They went down after him and captured fords of Jordan against Moab and did not allow a man to cross.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Follow after me: for the LORD hath delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand. And they went down after him, and took the fords of Jordan toward Moab, and suffered not a man to pass over.

modern.text: “Follow me,” he told them, “for the LORD has delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand.” So they followed him down and seized the fords of the Jordan leading to Moab, and did not allow anyone to cross over.

verses.restored: They struck Moab at that time about ten thousand men, every strong and every man of valor; no man escaped.

familiar.text: And they slew of Moab at that time about ten thousand men, all lusty, and all men of valour; and there escaped not a man.

modern.text: At that time they struck down about ten thousand Moabites, all robust and valiant men. Not one of them escaped.

original.text: וַיַּכּ֨וּ אֶת מוֹאָ֜ב בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא כַּעֲשֶׂ֤רֶת אֲלָפִים֙ אִ֔ישׁ כָּל שָׁמֵ֖ן וְכָל אִ֣ישׁ חָ֑יִל וְלֹ֥א נִמְלַ֖ט אִֽישׁ

modern.text: So Moab was subdued under the hand of Israel that day, and the land had rest for eighty years. Shamgar

verses.restored: After him was Shamgar son of Anath; he struck Philistine, six hundred men, with oxgoad; he also saved Israel.

familiar.text: And after him was Shamgar the son of Anath, which slew of the Philistines six hundred men with an ox goad: and he also delivered Israel.

modern.text: After Ehud came Shamgar son of Anath. And he too saved Israel, striking down six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad.

translation_notes: Verses 1-2 explain remaining nations as a test and a means of teaching war. This is descriptive theology within Judges and must not become a modern argument that young people need war to become faithful.
Intermarriage language is tied to cultic assimilation in the narrator's covenant frame and must not be used for racism, xenophobia, or anti-intermarriage ideology.
Othniel's story is brief and paradigmatic: cry, raised deliverer, Spirit, victory, quiet, death.
Ehud is described as 'restricted/bound in his right hand' or left-handed; the phrase should not be treated as disability shame. His difference becomes tactically significant in the narrative.
Eglon's fatness is part of the assassination scene's grotesque satire. Modern reception must reject body shaming and anti-fat mockery.

The Ehud narrative uses deception, assassination, toilet humor, and slaughter of fleeing Moabites. It may be preserved as ancient resistance narrative but not preached as a model for political murder.
Shamgar's oxgoad notice is terse, violent, and historically obscure; 'son of Anath' may carry complex cultural or divine-war associations requiring audit.
safety_note: Do not use Judges 3 to glorify assassination, mock fat bodies, shame disability, promote ethnic purity, or argue that war is spiritually necessary. Center the cry for deliverance, the danger of oppression, and careful refusal to turn survival violence into a general moral template.
